text:
STOPWORDS in tray.ts is shared with bodyKeywords; growing it rewrites stored triples

Adding a word to STOPWORDS changes what bodyKeywords stores, so every note's mentions triples change on the next re-drain. Put question-only words in QUERY_ONLY_STOPWORDS. Period phrases are excised from the question before tokenizing (temporalQuery returns a residual), so they never need a stopword. Pinned by the steward's PR #21 review.

The listener stays Core-free; core.spec pins the literal empty identity in listen.ts

helix/src/listen.ts senses under identity values [] goals [] style {} and must never import core.js or loadCore; test/core.spec.ts asserts the literal string. The dogfood sweep (sweepSpool in tray.ts) reuses senseBatch unchanged, and the drain re-screens every packet under the loaded Core afterwards.

Hit.matched must stay the query-token list; use Hit.via for the stored word a query word matched

buffer.spec, compound.spec and tray.spec pin matched with toContain and arrayContaining on query words like jordan, fixture, loader. Prefix matches (deploy finding deployment) are reported through via, never by replacing matched.

tray.ts and listen.ts must not import each other; shared pieces live in trace-io.ts and sources.ts

writeTrace moved to trace-io.ts and the read-only scanners (scanInbox, scanBufferText, scanBufferFile, scanSpool) to sources.ts so the tray can sweep the spool with listen.ts's drainSpool and processBatch without an import cycle. tray.ts re-exports writeTrace and scanInbox for older callers.

Fixture mtimes are checkout-dependent; tests that depend on file observation time must set utimesSync

git keeps no mtimes, so notes under helix/fixtures/tray are observed whenever the clone happened. A ranking pin on the fixtures must resolve on a single note, never on a tie, and any time-sensitive test writes its own notes and sets their mtime explicitly.

Working memory is a budget per pg-s2w pass; drainPackets perceives a larger backlog in rounds

slot_schema.maxSlots (64) bounds one sensory-to-working invocation, not the drain. Before commit 364b49e everything past the first 64 buffered packets was reported as deferred and never committed by a buffer drain. Now one pg-s2w and one pg-w2l pass run per 64 packets in source order and pg-audit runs once at the end; --max-slots sets the budget.

Every --dogfood CLI test must pass --spool --buffer --inbox --store and --core at temp paths

The sweep consumes spool files and the drain reads the Core; a spawn without those flags sweeps the developer's real ~/.mneme/spool and loads their core.json. dogfood.spec.ts shows the shape; assert stderr is empty so a non-zero exit shows why (steward review on PR #21).

What the steward pushed back on in PR #21 review: fail closed, one source of truth, hermetic, bounded, honest

Fail closed on an unused flag (--as-of with no period throws). Read a node's own output rather than recomputing outside the graph. Spawned tests pass --core and assert stderr empty. Cap output with an explicit and N more line. Label observation time honestly (file mtime versus adapter clock). Keep period vocabulary inside temporal-query.ts via a residual question. Qualify ordering claims in docs.

The scheduler routes declared edges only; rerank is identity and inject never sets need_more

Retrieval heuristics belong in the hybrid transform stand-in. rerank is a Core-constrained prompt node, so a heuristic there would masquerade as Core-aware. Setting inject.slots.need_more true would route the cyclic w12 edge on query-derived state and exercise the acknowledged cyclic re-arm debt. Never parse prompt text to choose an edge.

pg-adl is not schedulable from the IR: guards a6 and a7 reference tau, which no ingress declares

SPEC ISSUE 2 in AGENTS.md. Helix fails closed (evalGuard throws) and bun src/judge.ts --runtime prints BLOCKED-RUNTIME. The fix is a steward 0.11 pack; never invent a tau, never stuff cluster.cut or archive.sample events, and the two liveness rows must stay fail on every tray trace.

A human-utterance-only Core refuses agent-note packets; an empty Core admits them

bun run remember spools a packet with channel claude-code and kind agent-note. HUMAN_UTTERANCE_KINDS in tray.ts is note and user-prompt only, so the ValueFilter stand-in rejects agent notes with core.deny plus core.interrupt per item. Agents author candidates; the operator's Core decides.

Decision on record: a heading-less title is clipped at TITLE_MAX 120 on ingest; headings stay whole

sensory.ts clipTitle cuts the first line of a heading-less packet at 120 characters on a word boundary, nothing appended. Titles from headings and every heading are stored as written. The constant is the steward's to change (helix/PROPOSALS.md item 5); entries re-title on their next re-drain.

Buffer and inbox drain together in dogfood; buffer-first was an accident of increments, not a decision

dogfoodSource once took the buffer when it held packets and fell back to the inbox, so one hook packet hid ~/mneme-tray from bun run dogfood forever. Commit a2ad716 drains both, buffer first then inbox by name; ids never collide across channels.

Rejected tonight by three reviewers: a cross-hit also-mentioned keyword block and automatic buffer rotation

The keyword intersection reads as insight without being any; DOGFOOD.md commits to source notes and stored facts without a fabricated narrative. Rotation moves the operator's L0 file and decides the fate of Core-denied packets. Both are written up in helix/PROPOSALS.md rather than built.
